content: Do not store this medication in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. The information provided here was last updated in August 2024. Zidovudine has been associated with severe blood-related complications, including anemia (a reduction in red blood cells) and neutropenia (a reduction in white blood cells). These complications are more common in individuals with advanced HIV disease (AIDS). Such blood problems may necessitate blood transfusions or discontinuation of the medication. Your doctor will monitor your blood counts regularly through laboratory tests. It is crucial to attend all scheduled medical appointments. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms of anemia, such as unusual fatigue, difficulty breathing, weakness, bluish discoloration of fingernails or lips, pale skin, or a rapid heartbeat. A low white blood cell count can increase your susceptibility to serious, potentially fatal infections. This medication may also cause muscle-related issues, such as myopathy. In rare cases, zidovudine has been linked to severe, potentially fatal liver problems and a metabolic condition known as lactic acidosis. Seek immediate medical care if you develop symptoms of liver dysfunction, such as persistent nausea, abdominal pain, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Similarly, seek help if you experience symptoms of lactic acidosis, such as rapid breathing, drowsiness, or muscle aches. Zidovudine is used in combination with other HIV medications to manage HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, thereby improving the function of the immune system. This helps lower the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and enhances overall quality of life. In pregnant women, zidovudine is used to prevent the transmission of HIV to the unborn child. However, it is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your healthcare provider. Do not share personal items, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors, that may have come into contact with blood or other bodily fluids. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, typically 2 to 3 times daily. Swallow it with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) unless otherwise instructed. If using the liquid form, measure the dose carefully with a special measuring device or spoon. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For children, the dosage is also based on weight. Pregnant women may need to take this medication up to 5 times daily. Take zidovudine at least 2 hours before or after taking clarithromycin. For optimal results, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. It is essential to continue taking this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not skip doses, take more or less than prescribed, or stop taking it without consulting your doctor, even for a short period. Common side effects may include headache, nausea, vomiting, difficulty sleeping, or loss of appetite. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to combat pre-existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Loss of body fat, particularly in areas such as the face, arms, legs, and buttocks, may occur while taking this medication, and this effect may be permanent. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance on side effects. Before taking zidovudine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Liquid formulations may contain sugar, so caution is advised if you have diabetes or any condition requiring a restricted sugar intake. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant before using this medication. Treatment with zidovudine can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the elimination of zidovudine from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Do not take this medication with other products containing zidovudine. Check the labels of all your prescription medications to ensure they do not contain zidovudine. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as blood counts, liver function tests, viral load, and T-cell counts) should be performed regularly. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
